title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages of 'Analysis situs, première mouture', 1986). There is a set 𝔉 of 'figures' (think: tame or constructible subsets of a space), ordered by inclusion ≤. Inside it sits a subset 𝔐 ⊂ 𝔉 of elementary pieces ('strates'). Every figure F is described by its strata, and axioms C3/C4/C4bis say that a figure is determined by, and can be glued from, its restrictions to the M_i. Page 65 proved the key lemma: a figure F is disjoint from a family Φ = {H_i} of figures iff each stratum of F is.

Page 66 sets up a Galois connection (a polarity) built from the symmetric relation 'disjoint'.
- Definitions. For Φ ⊂ 𝔉, put 𝔉' = cosupp_𝔉(Φ) = {F ∈ 𝔉 | F ∩ H_i = ∅ for all H_i ∈ Φ}. Likewise 𝔐' = cosupp_𝔐(Φ) = {X ∈ 𝔐 | X disjoint from all H_i}, which equals 𝔐 ∩ cosupp_𝔉(Φ).
- Mutual determination. By the lemma of p.65, F ∈ 𝔉' ⟺ all strata of F lie in 𝔐' (written F ⊂ 𝔐'). Conversely 𝔐' = 𝔉' ∩ 𝔐. So 𝔉' and 𝔐' determine each other.
- Margin note. 𝔉' and 𝔐' are 'closed' parts of 𝔉 and 𝔐: hereditary, and stable under (finite) sup.
- Support. Define 𝔉'' = cosupp_𝔉(𝔉') =: supp_𝔉(Φ) and 𝔐'' = cosupp_𝔐(𝔉') =: supp_𝔐(Φ). Then 𝔉'' ⊃ Φ, and 𝔉'' is stable under sup and under passage to sub-objects.
- Reduction to strata. With Φ̄ = ⋃ H_i, one has cosupp_𝔉(Φ) = cosupp_𝔉(𝔐_Φ̄), where 𝔐_Φ̄ is the set of strata contained in Φ̄. Also cosupp_𝔐(Φ) = {X ∈ 𝔐 | X disjoint from every Y ∈ 𝔐_Φ̄}. So everything reduces to constructions inside 𝔐 with the disjointness relation on strata.
- Saturated parts. A part 𝔉_0 of 𝔉 is saturated if it equals the cosupport of its cosupport; likewise 𝔐_0 ⊂ 𝔐. These correspond bijectively via 𝔐_0 = 𝔉_0 ∩ 𝔐 and 𝔉_0 = {F | F ⊂ 𝔐_0}.

The next page completes the picture. Saturated parts are the closed elements of this Galois connection. cosupp is an inclusion-reversing involution on them. They form a complete lattice Σ of 'supports virtuels', with Inf = intersection and Sup = saturation of the union.

Purpose: to give an intrinsic, purely combinatorial notion of 'support' (and of complementary support) for figures in an axiomatic tame topology. This feeds the later treatment of contours, residual parts and π_0 in the stratified setting.
errors: No real error. The facts 𝔉'' ⊃ Φ and the anti-isomorphism on saturated parts use the symmetry of the relation 'disjoint', which holds but is not stated explicitly.
'Stable par sup' presumably means stable under finite sups (finite unions of figures). Arbitrary sups need not exist in 𝔉 unless gluing (C4bis) supplies them.
Writing F ⊂ 𝔐' means 'all strata of F belong to 𝔐''. This is a slight abuse of notation, relying on identifying a figure with its set of strata.

ideas.what: Cosupport of a family of figures: the set of figures disjoint from all of them. Support = cosupport of the cosupport. Saturated parts are the fixed points, and they form a complete lattice anti-isomorphic to itself under cosupp.
ideas.modern_name: Galois connection / polarity induced by an orthogonality (disjointness) relation; closure system; complete ortholattice. Topological analogue: regular open sets, int(cl(U)).
ideas.usually_credited_to: G. Birkhoff (polarities, Lattice Theory 1940); Ore (Galois connections, 1944). Orthogonality closures in quantum logic and orthomodular lattice theory.
ideas.where_published: Only in the unpublished Analysis situs notes (Montpellier cote 156). Tame topology as a programme appears in Esquisse d'un programme §5, but not this construction.

ideas.what: Reduction of cosupports in the set of figures to the set of strata, using the lemma that disjointness is tested stratum by stratum. Bijection between saturated parts of 𝔉 and of 𝔐.
ideas.modern_name: Restriction of a closure operator to a generating subset (join-dense basis); poset of strata of a stratified space.

ideas.what: 'Supports virtuels' Σ: an intrinsic lattice of supports attached to an axiomatic tame/stratified space.
ideas.modern_name: Lattice of closed sets of a disjointness polarity on the strata. Close to the Boolean algebra of regular opens in o-minimal or definable settings, or to concept lattices.
ideas.usually_credited_to: no single source for this specific form

missed.claim: Grothendieck's axiomatic tame-topology draft (1986) defines an intrinsic notion of support and 'virtual supports' via a disjointness Galois connection on figures and strata. This is part of an unpublished axiomatisation of 'analysis situs' that is not documented in the literature on tame topology. Mathematically it is routine lattice theory; the novelty is only historical.
missed.quote: Partie saturée de 𝔉 : égale au cosupport de son cosupport ... Elles se correspondent mutuellement par 𝔐_0 = 𝔉_0 ∩ 𝔐, 𝔉_0 = {F ∈ 𝔉 | F ⊂ 𝔐_0}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents how Grothendieck intended to build tame topology axiomatically: from figures, strata and disjointness, rather than from o-minimal structures. This is of interest to historians and to people comparing his programme with o-minimality.

deep.surprise_reason: Standard Galois-connection / orthogonality-closure construction applied to Grothendieck's own axiomatic framework of figures and strata. It is historically interesting as part of the unpublished Analysis situs, but mathematically elementary.
transcription_corrections: Top right reads something like '(cf J' / '(c J', a cross-reference to an axiom, not '(cf'.

The saturated-part line should read approximately: 'Partie saturée 𝔉_0 de 𝔉 : égale au cosupport de son cosupport (p.r. à 𝔉). Partie saturée 𝔐_0 de 𝔐 : égale au cosupport de son cosupport (dans 𝔐). Elles se correspondent mutuellement par ...'. The transcribed 'égale au cosupport (p.r. à F). Partie de son cosupport' is a misreading.
'et par passage : [...] sous-objets[?]' is most likely 'et par passage aux sous-objets'.
Left margin: 'ainsi, 𝔐' et 𝔉' se déterminent mutuellement' is correct.
The margin 'NB 𝔉', 𝔐' sont des parties fermées de 𝔉, 𝔐' is correct; the struck line below it is '𝔉' stables par sup.'
'Soit Φ̄ = ⋃_{H_i∈Φ} H_i' is correct. In 'cosupp_𝔐(Φ) = {X ∈ 𝔐 | X disjoint de tout Y ∈ 𝔐_Φ̄}', the 'disjoint de tout' is written 'disjoint de ∀'.
